items.question: On 31 March 2026, debtors (after write-offs) were ₹8,00,000: not yet due ₹5,00,000 (1% uncollectible), up to 30 days overdue ₹2,00,000 (5%), over 30 days overdue ₹1,00,000 (20%). Allowance A/c opened at ₹30,000 Cr; ₹18,000 of bad debts were written off against it. Bad debts expense for the year?
items.explanation: Required closing allowance by ageing is ₹35,000. The allowance already has a credit balance of ₹12,000 after the write-offs. Only the shortfall of ₹23,000 is charged to profit and loss as the year's expense.

why_not.C: Charged the full required allowance and ignored the existing credit balance.
why_not.A: Deducted the opening ₹30,000-18,000 wrongly, using only the write-offs, not the balance.
why_not.D: Added the existing ₹12,000 balance to the required allowance instead of deducting it.

items.exam_tip: Ageing method fixes the closing allowance; expense = required balance minus balance already in the allowance account.
items.reviewer_note: Write-offs assumed charged against the allowance (allowance method), stated in question.
check_notes: Writer: Write-offs assumed charged against the allowance (allowance method), stated in question.

items.question: Under SA 530, an auditor finds a deviation in a sample that seems caused by a one-off computer failure. To treat it as an anomaly, what must the auditor do?
options: Obtain a high degree of certainty it is not representative of the population
Exclude it without any further work
Treat it as proof that the control is ineffective
Extrapolate it to the whole population as a likely error
items.explanation: SA 530 defines an anomaly as a misstatement or deviation clearly not representative of the population. The auditor must obtain a high degree of certainty, by performing additional procedures, before treating an item as an anomaly.

why_not.B: Excluding it without extra work is wrong; certainty must come from specific procedures.
why_not.D: Extrapolation applies to genuine errors, not to a demonstrated anomaly.
why_not.C: One isolated, explained deviation does not automatically make the control ineffective.

items.exam_tip: Anomaly means clearly unrepresentative, and the auditor must prove it with high certainty, not assume it.
check_notes: Checker: The wrong options are weak. B, C and D are plainly incorrect, so a student who half-remembers SA 530 can still pick A by elimination. A stronger distractor would help, such as 'obtain management's written representation that the failure was isolated'.

Checker: Option A leaves out the standard's words 'by performing additional audit procedures' and 'in extremely rare circumstances'. The answer is still correct, but quoting the standard in full would be more precise.

items.question: A registered trader sells a festival hamper for a single price of ₹1,00,000 (excl. GST): sweets ₹40,000 (5% GST), crockery ₹40,000 (18% GST), exempt books ₹20,000. Items are not naturally bundled; no one item is principal. GST payable?
items.explanation: The hamper is a mixed supply (not naturally bundled, single price). It is taxed at the rate of the supply attracting the highest rate, 18%, on the whole price: 18% of ₹1,00,000.

why_not.D: Taxed each item at its own rate and ignored exempt books; that applies only to separate supplies.
why_not.A: Applied 18% only on the 5% and 18% items, leaving out the exempt books value.
why_not.B: Used the lowest rate of 5% on the whole price instead of the highest rate.

items.exam_tip: Composite: principal supply's rate. Mixed: highest-rate item's rate on the whole price.
items.applicability: CGST Act, 2017 (as per ICMAI notice, up to 30 Nov 2025)
items.reviewer_note: Rates are stated in the question. Rule is from the CGST Act provision on composite and mixed supplies (section 8).
check_notes: Writer: Rates are stated in the question. Rule is from the CGST Act provision on composite and mixed supplies (section 8).

Checker: The 18% rate for crockery may not match the post-September 2025 rate schedule (ceramic tableware was rationalised to a lower rate). This does not change the answer, because the question states the rates itself, but a real-world item with a disputed rate could confuse students. Consider calling it a generic item 'taxable at 18%'.
Checker: The phrase 'single price' together with 'no one item is principal' strongly signals a mixed supply, which comes close to giving the answer away.
Second checker: Wording such as 'not naturally bundled; no one item is principal' tells the student it is a mixed supply. This is minor.
Second checker: The question does not say the ₹1,00,000 is the whole value for GST purposes, but 'excl. GST' covers it.
